name: Mississippi
headline_status: Medical cannabis is legal for registered patients; recreational use remains illegal.
summary: Mississippi allows medical cannabis under the Mississippi Medical Cannabis Act, signed in February 2022 after the state Supreme Court threw out the voter-approved Initiative 65. Patients with qualifying conditions buy from licensed dispensaries; there is no home growing and no adult-use market. A first offense for possessing 30 grams or less is handled with a fine rather than jail. In 2026 the governor vetoed two bills that would have loosened the program, and override attempts failed.

medical_since.value: Mississippi Medical Cannabis Act (SB 2095) signed by Gov. Tate Reeves on February 2, 2022.

retail_sales.value: Medical dispensary sales began in January 2023; there are no adult-use sales.

medical_program.value: Patients need certification for a listed condition such as cancer, PTSD, Crohn's disease, sickle cell anemia or certain chronic pain; purchases are capped at about 3 ounces (84 g) per month, with flower limited to 30% THC.

home_grow.value: Not allowed for patients or caregivers.

public_use.value: Patients may not smoke or vape cannabis in public or in a motor vehicle.

taxes.value: 5% excise tax on the wholesale price, plus regular sales tax.

regulator.value: Mississippi State Department of Health runs the program, working with the Department of Revenue, which handles dispensaries.

penalties.value: Non-patients: a first offense for up to 30 grams brings a fine of up to $250; repeat offenses can bring jail time, and larger amounts are felonies.

possession_limit.value: No legal amount without a medical card. Patients may possess up to 28 equivalency units at a time (98 grams of flower, under 3.5 ounces) and buy no more than 6 units a week.

purchase_age.value: Medical only. Only MDs and DOs may certify minors, who need a parent's or guardian's consent, and patients under 21 cannot enter a dispensary without a parent or guardian.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Mississippi has no THC per se or zero-tolerance law, so a cannabis DUI requires evidence of impairment.

tourists.value: Medical patients only. Visitors with an active medical card from their home state can apply up to 30 days ahead for a 15-day nonresident card, then buy up to 6 units a week and 12 per 15 days; there are no adult-use sales.

timeline.event: Voters approve medical cannabis Initiative 65; the state Supreme Court later voids it along with the ballot initiative process.
Gov. Reeves signs the Mississippi Medical Cannabis Act.
Gov. Reeves vetoes HB 895 and HB 1152, which would have eased program rules; override attempts fail.

faq.a: Only for registered medical patients. Recreational use is illegal.

faq.q: Who qualifies for medical marijuana in Mississippi?
faq.a: Patients certified for a qualifying condition, such as cancer, PTSD, Crohn's disease, sickle cell anemia, or chronic pain that meets the law's definition.
Partly. A first offense for 30 grams or less is punished by a fine of up to $250, but repeat offenses can bring jail time.

faq.q: Can you grow your own medical marijuana in Mississippi?
faq.a: No. Patients and caregivers must buy from licensed dispensaries.
